item.title: [PHOTOS] Nigeria Re-Elected To Council Of International Telecommunication Union
item.description: Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar. With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030. As part of Nigeria’s campaign for re-election, the Ambassador to Qatar Mahmood Yakubu (right) had a bilateral meeting with Mr. Jijun Xiong, China’s Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology and Leader of the Chinese delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) conference (Doha 2026). Established in 1865 with headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, the ITU is the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies (ICTs). It brings together 194 member states and over 1,000 sector members, which include companies, universities and international organisations. Nigeria became a member in 1961. Nigeria’s participation was coordinated by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu. The Nigerian delegation was led by the Minister of Communication, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani. With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030. Nigeria’s Ambassador to the State of Qatar, Mahmood Yakubu, served as the Deputy Head of Delegation, supported by the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Aminu Maida; Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to Geneva, led by Innocent Imejuo; officials of the Ministry of Communication (NCC) and staff of the Nigerian Embassy in Doha. item.title: COAS, Tinubu seek technology-driven security cooperation
item.description: The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on Monday joined President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the opening of the Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja, where participants called for stronger intelligence collaboration and technology-driven security operations. The conference, held on November 16, 2026, at the Armed Forces Officers’ Mess, Asokoro, was themed, “Optimizing Intelligence Through Technological Innovations and Strategic Partnerships in a Complex Security Environment.” President Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, emphasised the need for stronger intelligence sharing, technological innovation and operational cooperation among security agencies to address emerging security threats. The President also urged security agencies to deepen partnerships with global technology companies and research institutions to strengthen the country’s intelligence-gathering and security capabilities. He further charged Nigerian Defence Advisers serving abroad to maximise bilateral and multilateral engagements to advance the country’s national security interests. The conference attracted top government and military officials, including the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.); the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede; Service Chiefs; senior government officials and Defence Advisers. The gathering focused on the role of emerging technologies, intelligence sharing and strategic partnerships in improving the country’s response to evolving security challenges. The participation of the COAS and other military leaders reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to strengthening a technology-enabled and intelligence-driven security architecture through inter-agency collaboration and strategic partnerships. The initiative is aimed at enhancing operational effectiveness and safeguarding Nigeria’s national security. item.title: British Singer Raye Tops 2027 Grammy With 11 Nominations
item.description: Soulful British singer-songwriter Raye on Monday topped the Grammy nominations with 11, and Spanish superstar Rosalía earned nine in a strong showing for female artists across the board. Women have historically been underrepresented at the Grammy Awards held by the Recording Academy, whose 69th annual gala will take place on February 7 in Los Angeles. Spanish singer-songwriter and actress Rosalia attends the 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada on November 12, 2026. Photo by CHRIS DELMAS / AFP But recent years have seen women dominate both the industry and the trophies list. Raye’s whopping 11 nominations included the three most prestigious, recognizing best album, best song, and best record for her jazz-inflected blend of pop and R&B. She was also recognized for her songwriting for fellow artists with a nomination for the relatively new best songwriter category. Rosalia’s nine nominations follow a banner night at last week’s Latin Grammys, where her sweeping, avant-garde classical pop album “Lux” reigned supreme. First-time nominee Ella Langley, the crooner behind the ubiquitous smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” will enter the evening with seven shots at Grammys gold, as will fellow country star Miranda Lambert, who co-wrote that hit and notably scooped a nomination for producer of the year. Pop-rock phenom Olivia Rodrigo also earned seven nods, as did the multifaceted musician Phoebe Bridgers, who released her third solo studio album “Lost Weekend” to widespread critical acclaim. First-timers make waves Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean — the English singer behind the smash “Man I Need” — earned six nods as did perennial Academy favorite Bruno Mars. Taylor Swift predictably will be a threat in the top categories for her album “The Life of a Showgirl” as well as the song she penned for the latest film in the “Toy Story” franchise. She has five chances at winning. But for all the heavyweight glory, it also proved a strong Grammys cycle for first-time nominees. New York indie rockers Geese capped a breakout year with their first-ever nominations, garnering five. Langley is a strong favorite for the Best New Artist category, but a crop of performers including Geese as well as brash electropop star Slayyyter and Canadian rock duo Angine de Poitrine could pull upsets. The new blood will be joined by stalwarts of the trade who earned nominations including Madonna, Paul McCartney, Bruce Springsteen and The Rolling Stones. The 2027 line-up features 100 competitive categories. The Grammy Awards will air on the US network ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu — the first time in half-a-century that the ceremony won’t be broadcast by CBS. item.title: Atiku thanks Yobe people for warm campaign reception
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has thanked the people of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception accorded him and his campaign team during the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in the state. Atiku also commended Yobe State Governor for providing what he described as a level playing field for the party to present its campaign message to the electorate. The former vice-president’s appreciation was contained in a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, who personally signed and posted it on his X account. Atiku said the reception he received from the moment his entourage arrived in Potiskum from Azare, Bauchi State, was a testament to the people’s support for the ADC’s campaign promise of an affordable life. “The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart. “To the people of Potiskum and to the good people of Yobe State, I say thank you. You opened your doors and your hearts to us, and we are deeply grateful,” he said. He also thanked the state governor for allowing the ADC to campaign freely, saying democracy was strengthened when political parties were given the opportunity to engage voters and present their programmes. Atiku, however, used the statement to take a swipe at the Presidency over allegations of the use of artificial intelligence to portray large crowds at political events. “The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate,” he said. He added that the ADC’s campaign did not need artificial crowds, insisting that the turnout and chants at its rallies reflected the people’s desire for political change. Atiku also referred to chants of “Tinubu Must Go” at ADC rallies, describing them as a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that would accompany a popular mandate. He pledged that, if elected president in the January 16, 2027 election, he would take immediate steps to make life more affordable for Nigerians. “When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow. I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president,” he said. Atiku said the reception in Yobe had reinforced his campaign’s belief that messages addressing the people’s everyday struggles and aspirations would attract widespread support. “Yobe has reminded us that when a message speaks to people’s struggles and aspirations, they will come out in their numbers to be heard,” he added. item.title: Plateau: People may forgive Tinubu, but won’t forget absence – Atiku
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recent appeal for forgiveness in Plateau State, saying the people may forgive him but will not forget his alleged failure to visit and stand with them during periods of killings and kidnappings. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said no campaign visit or last-minute promise could erase what he described as the President’s absence when Plateau residents needed reassurance and protection. He spoke through a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, who disclosed the position on his X platform. The statement was issued from Potiskum, Yobe State, where Atiku took his affordable-life campaign message on Sunday. According to the former Vice President, Plateau residents needed the President’s presence when their communities were under attack and families were grieving over the loss of loved ones. “The people of Plateau needed their President when they were grieving, when their communities were under attack and when families desperately needed reassurance. “President Tinubu promised to end the killings and protect them, but he failed to keep those promises. He did not visit to stand with them in their darkest hour,” Atiku said. He argued that Tinubu’s recent visit to the state to seek political support could not erase the concerns over his response to the security challenges confronting the people. “Now he has gone to Plateau to campaign and ask for forgiveness. The people may forgive him, but they will never forget the lives lost, the communities left in fear and the absence of their President when they needed him most,” he said. Atiku added that residents should not be treated as campaign instruments, insisting that their grief should not be used for political purposes. “President Tinubu cannot abandon Plateau in its hour of agony, then return when he needs its votes and expect a warm welcome. “The people are not props for his campaign, and their grief is not a slogan to be used when politically convenient. They may forgive him, but they will remember—and they will hold him accountable,” he added. The ADC presidential candidate also extended his criticism to the Tinubu administration’s handling of the economy, accusing the President of failing to address the cost-of-living crisis confronting Nigerians. He said the President had failed to meet the expectations of Nigerians who gave him the mandate in the 2023 general election. Atiku, however, presented the ADC’s Affordable Life campaign as an alternative, saying it was designed to address the country’s economic challenges and restore relief, dignity and hope to households. “Nigerians deserve leadership that stands with them in their moments of greatest hardship,” he said. item.title: Obi demands arrest of attackers of Kwankwaso’s convoy in Kano
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has called for an immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for the attack on the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. Obi, who disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Monday, said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised during the incident. He condemned the attack, describing it as unacceptable and warning against the growing resort to violence during political activities. “I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. “I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” he said. Obi said political differences should not be used as justification for violence, intimidation or destruction of property, stressing that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack. “Democracy is not warfare. Political differences should never be a reason to resort to violence, intimidation or the destruction of property,” he stated. He urged Nigerians to embrace dialogue and respect divergent political opinions, warning that violence could undermine democratic participation. The former governor specifically called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those involved and prosecute anyone found culpable, including alleged sponsors of the attack. “I therefore call on the Nigeria Police Force and all relevant security agencies to immediately investigate this incident, identify those responsible, including anyone found to have sponsored the attack, and ensure that they are brought to justice. “No individual should be above the law, regardless of political position or influence,” he said. Obi also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and others affected by the incident, while wishing those injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed his commitment to peaceful political engagement, saying the quest for political change should be pursued through dialogue, persuasion, ideas and the ballot rather than violence. “Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence,” he added. item.title: Tinubu’s proximity won’t make me dictate Katsina politics – Masari
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Political Affairs, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, has dismissed suggestions that he is using his closeness to the President to influence or dictate the political direction of Katsina State. Masari, who spoke in an interview with the BBC Hausa Service, also said he had no regrets supporting Dr Dikko Radda’s emergence as governor of Katsina State, despite reported political differences between them. His comments come amid speculations that the strained relationship between him and Radda could affect the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. The presidential aide said President Tinubu and Almighty Allah were witnesses to his contributions towards Radda’s emergence, lamenting what he described as unfair allegations against him. Asked to assess Radda’s performance in office over the past three years, Masari said even those opposed to the governor would acknowledge that he had made efforts to develop the state. “I have no regrets helping Dikko Radda to become the Governor of Katsina State,” he declared. Explaining the origin of the disagreement, Masari alleged that the crisis began when some youths associated with the governor started displaying campaign materials bearing Radda’s photograph without that of President Tinubu. He said he, alongside a minister and another prominent Katsina politician, Malam Jabiru Tsauri, had mobilised resources to promote the President and other political leaders in the state. According to him, they sponsored billboards, posters and banners across Katsina featuring photographs of Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima, Governor Radda, former governors Aminu Masari and Ibrahim Shehu Shema, among other prominent political figures. Masari alleged that some of the billboards were subsequently destroyed at night by individuals he claimed were working with the governor’s aides. He further claimed that some suspects were arrested by the police in connection with the incident, adding that the development contributed to the misunderstanding between the two camps. “I don’t have any issue with the governor; perhaps he has one with me. But what I will disagree with is a situation where the President cannot be advertised in Katsina State,” he said. Masari also alleged that some individuals around the governor were uncomfortable with him and were responsible for creating tension between the two political camps. He maintained that Radda should not feel threatened by the political activities of Katsina indigenes residing in Abuja, insisting that he and other prominent politicians from the state had no personal or political problem with the governor. He urged APC stakeholders to ensure that the perceived divisions did not undermine the party’s unity and electoral fortunes in Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027 Grammys: Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr, Wizkid Earn Nominations
item.description: Afrobeats stars Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr and Wizkid have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Nigerian artistes featuring prominently across several categories. The Recording Academy announced the nominations on Monday, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple nods in the Best African Music Performance and Best Global Music categories. Tems leads the Nigerian contingent with four nominations, while Asake earned two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category. Other Nigerian artistes recognised include Davido, Ayra Starr, Burna Boy and Wizkid, who shares a nomination with Asake. In the Best African Music Performance category, Nigerian artistes account for four of the five nominated entries. Mandatory Credit: Photo by MJ Photos/REX/Shutterstock Grammy Awards 60th Annual Grammy Awards, Press Room, New York, USA – 28 Jan 2018 Asake earned nominations for his songs ‘Gratitude’ and ‘Jogodo’, his collaboration with Wizkid. Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr received a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’. The fifth nominee is Ghanaian musician King Ayisoba, whose song ‘No Tradition, No Africa’ features Rocky Dawuni. Tems also received nominations in three other categories. She was recognised in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for ‘What You Need’, as well as Best Global Music Album for her project, Love Is a Kingdom. Ayra Starr earned another nomination in the Best Global Music Album category for Starrgirl, while Davido’s Oriadé was also nominated in the category. Burna Boy received a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira. Other International Stars British singer-songwriter RAYE emerged as the biggest winner among international artistes at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, leading all nominees with 11 nominations. Her recognition includes Album of the Year for ‘This Music May Contain Hope’, as well as Record and Song of the Year for ‘Where Is My Husband!’ and Songwriter of the Year. Spanish singer Rosalía followed with nine nominations, including Album of the Year for ‘Lux (Complete Works)’ and Record and Song of the Year for ‘Berghain’, her collaboration with Björk and Yves Tumor. Other major international contenders include American singer Olivia Rodrigo and country star Ella Langley, who each earned seven nominations, while British singer Olivia Dean secured six. Phoebe Bridgers and Miranda Lambert also received seven nominations each, while Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas earned six apiece. Taylor Swift received five nominations, including recognition in the major categories for her album ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ and songs ‘The Fate of Ophelia’ and ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’. item.title: Oyo proposes N1.115trn 2027 budget, targets jobs, infrastructure
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has proposed a N1.115 trillion budget for 2027, prioritising infrastructure development, job creation, entrepreneurship and the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate economic expansion and improve residents’ living standards. The proposed budget, tagged “Budget of Sustained Progress,” is designed to consolidate gains recorded across critical sectors while strengthening the state’s economic competitiveness through investments in infrastructure, agriculture, human capital development and public-private partnerships. Governor Seyi Makinde presented the proposal to the Oyo State House of Assembly last week, with capital expenditure accounting for 60.1 per cent of the total spending plan. Speaking during the presentation of the budget breakdown and analysis at the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning in Ibadan on Monday, the Permanent Secretary, Julius Ayanleke, said the proposal aligned with the administration’s vision of making Oyo State the fastest-growing economy in Nigeria. He said the government’s spending priorities would focus on completing ongoing projects, strengthening Internally Generated Revenue (IGR), attracting public and private investments, supporting MSMEs, expanding infrastructure and ensuring efficient utilisation of resources through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). According to Ayanleke, the proposed budget comprises N670.03 billion for capital expenditure, representing 60.1 per cent, and N445.31 billion for recurrent expenditure, accounting for the remaining 39.9 per cent. He explained that the substantial allocation to capital projects was intended to sustain the state’s development drive, particularly through the completion of ongoing projects and execution of critical infrastructure programmes. Among the projects earmarked for priority funding are the Ibadan Circular Road, Ido-Eruwa Road and several rural road projects, which he said had received adequate provisions to facilitate their timely completion. Providing an update on the state’s fiscal performance, Ayanleke disclosed that Oyo generated N618.72 billion between January and September 2026. He said the revenue comprised N401.44 billion in recurrent revenue and N217.28 billion in capital receipts. The permanent secretary explained that the 2027 budget was developed through the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), sectoral planning processes and consultations with stakeholders across the state’s seven geopolitical zones to ensure that the spending priorities reflected residents’ development needs. Outlining the government’s fiscal targets, he said the administration would prioritise the completion of ongoing projects, reduce non-essential overhead costs and improve efficiency in personnel and recurrent expenditure. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’ll get over 80% votes in Ebonyi, Nwifuru vows
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Governor Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has vowed to deliver more than 80 per cent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, citing what he described as the President’s contributions to the state and its people. Nwifuru said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to Ebonyi through key appointments, particularly the appointment of former Governor David Umahi as Minister of Works. The governor spoke during the inauguration of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT) Door-to-Door Campaign Movement at Unity Square, Abakaliki, where he also commended the group’s initiator, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, for mobilising support for the President’s re-election. He described Umahi’s appointment as a significant recognition of the South-East, noting that the region had not previously occupied the position of Minister of Works. “Most importantly, like we said during the presidential campaign inauguration here, he has appointed our son, our brother, our ally, our father, the Minister of Works of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. And he is a true supporter of our dear President. “I am feeling very, very grateful to our dear brother, Tompolo, for this show of love and show of gratitude,” he said. Nwifuru described Tinubu as an exceptional leader who had supported youths and other Nigerians, adding that his administration’s actions had strengthened the state’s commitment to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He said the President’s appointments and other interventions had convinced the people of Ebonyi to support his re-election bid. “We do not want anybody to embarrass us because what the President has done to us has convinced us. And we are ready to vote for him beyond 80 per cent. “Our people are well educated. They are well enlightened. They are aware of the sacrifices Mr President has made,” the governor said. He also urged residents to vote massively for APC candidates in the 2027 elections, describing the party’s performance in the state as deserving of electoral support. “And the party has done tremendously well for our people here. We are indebted to the party. And to pay the party back is to vote for APC party massively from top to bottom,” he added. Speaking at the event, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Tompolo, who was represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Kestin Pondi, said the movement was established to take the President’s re-election campaign directly to households across the country. Pondi described Tinubu as a courageous leader who had embarked on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration and sustained them despite the challenges. item.title: Only 14 states pay pensions regularly – PenCom
item.description: The National Pension Commission (PenCom) has disclosed that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states are meeting their pension obligations regularly, raising concerns over persistent delays in the payment of retirement benefits by several state governments. The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, disclosed this during an interview with ARISE NEWS on Monday, acknowledging that some states were performing poorly in meeting their pension obligations to retirees. “We have 14 states that are paying up. But 14 out of 36 states is a lot. And some states are doing very badly,” she said. Oloworaran, however, did not identify the states making regular payments or those defaulting on their pension obligations. On the Federal Government’s minimum pension initiative, the PenCom chief disclosed that the ₦400bn provided by the Federal Government and the pension industry for the Pension Protection Fund could sustain the programme for at least 10 years based on current projections. She explained that the Federal Government contributed ₦350bn, while the pension industry provided ₦50bn. According to her, the commission had engaged an actuary to assess the financial requirements of the initiative and determine its long-term sustainability. “Conservatively, we’re good for the next 10 years. Conservatively,” she said. She, however, noted that the projections could be reviewed in response to inflation and the funds available to support the programme. Oloworaran assured that the commission remained committed to ensuring that vulnerable retirees continued to receive financial support under the minimum pension arrangement. She further disclosed that the Pension Protection Fund had a balance of ₦38bn before the current administration, adding that part of the Federal Government’s contribution was intended to clear outstanding pension backlogs. She said 54 per cent of beneficiaries who had received payments under the initiative were private-sector retirees, while nearly 70 per cent of workers expected to qualify for the programme were also from the private sector. Police pension dispute On the controversy surrounding retired police officers seeking to exit the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) and return to the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS), Oloworaran said PenCom was working with the police to develop an arrangement that would safeguard their retirement savings. She disclosed that different options had been presented to President Bola Tinubu for consideration, stressing that the priority was to ensure improved pension benefits for police retirees without jeopardising their funds. “But what we want to do is put a structure in place. Where we are sure that nothing at all will happen to the funds for our police,” she said. According to her, the ultimate objective was to ensure that retired police officers received higher pension benefits, irrespective of the arrangement eventually adopted. “And the ultimate result is more money in the hands of police. item.title: MSF: Shortage of diphtheria drugs fuelling outbreak in Northern Nigeria
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned that shortages of diphtheria antitoxin (DAT), a critical drug for treating the disease, coupled with low immunisation coverage, are fuelling transmission and undermining efforts to contain the outbreak in northern Nigeria. The international medical humanitarian organisation said the situation was putting thousands of children at risk of severe illness and death, calling on the Federal and state governments, donors and international partners to urgently address shortages of essential medicines and vaccines. MSF Medical Coordinator in Nigeria, Dr David Kizito, raised the alarm in a statement made available to our correspondent in Maiduguri on Monday. He urged relevant authorities and international partners to secure available supplies of diphtheria antitoxin, vaccines and other essential medicines, ensure their timely clearance at ports of entry and facilitate rapid distribution to affected communities across northern Nigeria. Diphtheria is a life-threatening but vaccine-preventable bacterial disease transmitted mainly through respiratory droplets and contact with infected wounds. Kizito described the global shortage of diphtheria antitoxin as a serious threat to the treatment of patients, warning that dwindling stocks could leave medical teams unable to save lives as the outbreak persists. “The global shortage of diphtheria antitoxin is becoming a matter of life and death. Our stocks are dangerously low, and we risk being unable to treat children and save lives as the outbreak continues. “Diphtheria is a preventable disease, yet children continue to arrive at health facilities with life-threatening complications because they are not fully vaccinated or cannot access care in time,” he said. He explained that diphtheria antitoxin was the only specific treatment capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the disease. Although included in the World Health Organisation’s Model List of Essential Medicines, he said its global availability remained inconsistent. According to him, the drug is most effective when administered within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms, but inadequate supplies have repeatedly forced MSF medical teams to ration treatment, potentially compromising patients’ outcomes. The statement said Nigeria had been battling a major diphtheria outbreak since late 2022, with the cumulative toll exceeding 41,000 suspected cases, more than 24,000 confirmed infections and over 1,260 deaths nationwide. It identified Bauchi, Borno, Kaduna, Katsina, Kano, Plateau, Sokoto and Zamfara as among the northern states particularly affected by the outbreak, with several areas recording recent increases in cases. In 2026 alone, as of August 9, Nigeria had recorded 12,977 suspected cases, 10,476 confirmed infections and 406 deaths, according to the organisation. item.description: Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, hosted Nigeria’s history-making Flamingos at a grand dinner reception at Lagos House, Marina, on Sunday, where he announced a N300 million reward package for the team. ‎Each of the 21 players and nine members of the coaching and backroom staff will receive N10 million. ‎The U-17 players also received an iPhone 18 Pro Max and customised headphones, while members of the technical crew received bespoke outfits and other gifts. ‎The reception drew government officials, sports administrators, family members and supporters, all of whom turned out to celebrate the newly-minted world champions. ‎Sanwo-Olu congratulated the team for putting Nigeria on the world map, describing their victory as a product of hard work, discipline and belief. NigerianNewspaper Access. ‎He urged the young players not to rest on their laurels but to remain focused on their education and football careers, assuring them that Lagos would continue to support sports development and reward excellence. Governor Sanwo-Olu with Flamingos. ‎The governor also praised head coach Akeem Ishola Busari and his technical crew for guiding the team to glory. ‎The Flamingos became the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco, on November 7. ‎Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored the goals that secured Nigeria’s maiden title in the competition. ‎One of the evening’s emotional moments came when captain Harmony Chidi knelt before the governor to express gratitude on behalf of the team. ‎Five members of the squad are from Robo Queens of Mushin, Lagos, highlighting the state’s contribution to the team’s success. ‎The Lagos reward follows the Federal Government’s reception for the team in Abuja, where President Bola Tinubu approved a N100 million Federal Government Savings Bond for each player. ‎The head coach received N100 million in cash, while other members of the technical and administrative crew received N50 million each. item.title: Keep politics out of Churches, Soludo cautions politicians
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into campaign arenas, insisting that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of different political persuasions. Soludo gave the warning on Sunday during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry, founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor urged religious leaders to maintain a clear distinction between politics and worship, stressing that places of worship should provide an atmosphere where everyone could freely seek God without political interference. According to him, churches should remain holy places where people of different political affiliations can worship peacefully. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. The governor recalled that about six months before his election, he deliberately resolved not to use any church platform to solicit votes or campaign for political support. He said he maintained the decision by worshipping at the Government House chapel throughout the period leading to the election and after. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the Government House chapel until the election day and afterwards,” he stated. Soludo reiterated his opposition to the politicisation of religious institutions, urging politicians to keep campaign activities away from churches and other places of worship. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message and it is my kind of consistency of character,” he added. item.title: Hardship real, but Nigeria is more than its challenges — Abbas
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has acknowledged the hardship confronting Nigerians, saying governments at all levels must urgently address the difficulties facing households and businesses. Abbas, however, cautioned the international community against defining Nigeria solely by its challenges, insisting that the country’s economic potential, human capital and development progress should also be recognised. He spoke on Monday at the ongoing Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, where he addressed issues bordering on responsible communication, democratic accountability, governance and institutional reforms. The Speaker, who was represented by the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians could no longer be ignored or dismissed. “The difficulties confronting households and businesses are real and deserve serious attention,” he said. Abbas noted that Nigerians expected improved security, employment opportunities, efficient public services and better governance, adding that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms must begin to reflect in their daily lives. He said the reforms being implemented by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration were designed to address structural weaknesses, restore economic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth. However, he acknowledged that the reforms had come with immediate costs, stressing that government had a responsibility to ensure that their eventual benefits translated into tangible improvements in citizens’ living conditions. “The challenge before government is to ensure that their benefits translate into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians,” he said. On insecurity, the Speaker called for decisive and sustained action against those responsible for violence across the country. He described every innocent life lost to insecurity as a tragedy that demanded justice and accountability. “Every innocent life lost is a tragedy that calls for justice and accountability,” he said. Abbas urged the country to remain resolute in confronting perpetrators of violence, strengthening security institutions and protecting every citizen, irrespective of religion, ethnicity or place of origin. Turning to Nigeria’s international image, the Speaker warned against narratives that portray the country exclusively through its difficulties, arguing that such representations could overshadow its achievements and development potential. “There is a difference between reporting a country’s difficulties and reducing the country to those difficulties. There is also a difference between legitimate scrutiny and the construction of narratives that oversimplify complex realities. “We do not seek immunity from scrutiny. item.title: Toluwanisings: Defendant fails to meet bail conditions, spends weekend in correctional centre
item.description: Joshua Oladipupo, a defendant, facing trial over alleged posting of fake news on the death of gospel singer, Bayonile Olayemi, popularly called Toluwanisings, failed to perfect his bail and spent the weekend at Agodi Correctional Centre, Ibadan. Investigation by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday revealed that Oladipupo, arraigned at the Iyaganku Magistrates’ Court in Ibadan on Friday, was yet to meet his bail conditions. The defendant, who was arraigned on a three-count charge of publication of fake news and conduct likely to cause breach of the peace, spent the weekend at the Agodi Correctional Centre. He had pleaded not guilty to the charges, and the magistrate, Mrs Oluwabusayo Osho, granted him N2 million bail with two sureties. Osho had also directed that the two sureties must be of close blood relations and must have landed properties within the jurisdiction of the court. She further held that the lands must possess Certificates of Occupancy (C of O) and survey documents. The magistrate subsequently ordered that the defendant be remanded at Agodi Correctional centre pending the perfection of the bail and adjourned the case until Dec. 17 for hearing. Earlier, the prosecutor, Insp Adeshina Folaranmi, had told the court that the defendant committed the offences in October 2026 in the Dugbe area of Ibadan. Folaranmi alleged that the defendant published fake news on Facebook and other social media handles about the death of a gospel singer, Bayonile Olayemi, popularly called Toluwanisings. He alleged that the defendant falsely published that the late singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo; wife, Damilola; and members of the deceased’s mother’s family were responsible for his death. The prosecutor alleged that the defendant’s intent was to cause fear and alarm to the public. Folaranmi said the offences contravened provisions of Sections 59 and 249(d) of the Criminal Laws of Oyo State, 2000. A NAN correspondent in court on Monday learnt that the defendant was still in custody because he had yet to meet the bail conditions. A reliable source, who preferred to speak on condition of anonymity, said that Oladipupo remained in custody pending meeting bail conditions set by the court. (NAN) The post Toluwanisings: Defendant fails to meet bail conditions, spends weekend in correctional centre appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Radda Welcomes Katsina ADC Defectors To APC
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will significantly surpass its 2023 electoral performance in the 2027 general elections, citing the party’s growing acceptance and expanding grassroots support across the state. Governor Radda made the declaration on Monday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally held at the Lazio Football Ground in Zango Local Government Area as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. The rally attracted thousands of party supporters and witnessed the defection of members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the APC, further strengthening the ruling party’s campaign drive ahead of the elections. Addressing the crowd, Governor Radda urged residents to remain steadfast in their support for the APC and cautioned them against what he described as “business politicians” whose objective, he said, was to undermine the achievements of the ruling party for personal interests. He called on the electorate to vote for APC candidates at all levels to sustain the administration’s development agenda. Zamfara Govenor Radda welcomes ADC defectors to APC. According to the governor, his administration has made significant investments in healthcare, education, agriculture, youth employment, economic development and security, while also providing subsidised fertiliser to farmers across the state to boost food production and improve livelihoods. “Beware of business politicians. APC will not disappoint you. We will continue to do more for our people. We have constructed hospitals, employed youths, strengthened education, agriculture, the economy and security. We have also distributed subsidised fertiliser to farmers across the state and remain committed to improving the living standards of our citizens,” Governor Radda said. “Ensure that you vote APC from top to bottom so that we can continue the good work we have started.” Also speaking, the Katsina State APC Deputy Chairman, Bala Abu Musawa, described the APC as a youth-focused party committed to creating greater opportunities for young people. He urged voters to support the party in the 2027 elections to consolidate ongoing development initiatives and deliver improved governance. Former Secretary to the Katsina State Government and former APC governorship aspirant, Dr. Mustapha Muhammad Inuwa, maintained that no opposition party could match the APC’s popularity and performance in the state. He alleged that critics of the ruling party were being dishonest and claimed that the ADC was facing internal legal and leadership challenges. Dr. Inuwa further urged residents to align themselves with the APC, saying the party remained the strongest political platform in Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Britain’s Prince William In India For Earthshot Prize
item.description: Britain’s Prince William played street cricket and took a metro ride in India’s financial capital, Mumbai, on Monday ahead of hosting his environmental Earthshot Prize, on a visit that will also include a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The future king, accompanied by his wife Princess Catherine, took part in India’s beloved game of “gully” cricket with batting legend Sachin Tendulkar in the Ballard Estate area of the city. Britain’s Prince William, Prince of Wales (L) and his wife Britain’s Kate, Princess of Wales (C) arrive with India’s former cricket player Sachin Tendulkar (R) for a game of gully cricket at the iconic Ballard Estate in Mumbai on November 16, 2026. (Photo by Indranil MUKHERJEE / AFP) The princess, dressed in a lime-green blazer and white trousers, tried her hand at batting before posing for photographs with young local players. The three-day visit is the first official overseas trip undertaken together by the couple in four years, with Catherine’s cancer diagnosis and treatment limiting international travel. The royal couple also hopped on for a ride in the city’s metro train to highlight sustainable travel. “Catherine and I are delighted to be in India for this year’s Earthshot Prize,” the Prince of Wales said in a social media post. Britain’s Prince William, Prince of Wales (L) and his wife Britain’s Kate, Princess of Wales (R) enter an Aqua Line metro train at Vidhan Bhavan station in Mumbai on November 16, 2026. (Photo by Punit PARANJPE / AFP) The prize, which supports innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges, selects five winners from 15 finalists in categories covering nature conservation, ocean protection, waste reduction, climate action and clean air. Each winner will receive £1 million ($1.3 million) at Tuesday night’s ceremony to expand their work. Hosted by filmmaker Karan Johar, the event is expected to draw Oscar-winning actor Rami Malek and Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor. William said that India had “become one of the most exciting places in the world for environmental innovation, with people across the country developing practical solutions to some of the greatest challenges we all share”. “I am very appreciative that the royal family has taken up such a noble cause,” Tendulkar, international cricket’s all-time leading run-scorer, told reporters. ‘Great challenges’ The clean-air category includes Indian vehicle manufacturer Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, which is expanding its electric three-wheeler business.
